title: APIs accepting rotated API keys due to proxy acceptance-window off-by-one
creator: Ava Chen
description: Production customers reported intermittent 401/200 anomalies after a scheduled API key rotation. Investigation found an acceptance-window off-by-one bug in egress proxy token validation that allowed some rotated API keys to be accepted for ~30s after rotation, and in other cases caused freshly rotated keys to be rejected. This ticket tracks the hotfix, rollout, and follow-ups across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
reproducer:
1) Deploy new API key and rotate via /admin/keys for org 'acme' on a canary proxy.
2) Simulate requests through edge-proxy instances with NTP skew +/- 1s and simultaneous cache flush.
3) Observe acceptance of both old and new keys for ~30s, or rejection depending on leader election timing.
Notes: reproduces locally with proxy clock offset +1s and token-acceptance-window configured at 30s.
root_cause: Edge-proxy validation uses an inclusive timestamp check against the 'valid_after' marker. During rotation we set the new key's valid_after to now, but upstream leader election and slight clock skew created a window where the proxy's comparator returned true for both old and new keys. Additionally, a signed-time canonicalization routine truncated sub-second data introducing an off-by-one second acceptance window in some runtimes. Two contributing factors: (1) acceptance comparator logic incorrectly used <= instead of < for transitional checks, (2) canonicalization rounding for epoch timestamps dropped sub-second precision in the proxy build shipped to Dedicated nodes.
mitigation: Emergency mitigation applied 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC: 1) Temporarily disabled cross-proxy cache coalescing to force authoritative lookup from central auth-service. 2) Rolled forward a config that tightened accept-window to 0s during rotations. 3) Notified affected Dedicated customers and enabled manual key revocation where necessary. All mitigations validated on staging then rolled to production canaries before broader rollout.
resolution_plan:
Short-term: merge and roll edge-proxy PR that fixes comparator to use strict < for new-key transient acceptance and reintroduces 3-digit millisecond precision in timestamp canonicalization (PR #4120). Patch auth-service to emit monotonic rotation tokens (PR #5421). Deploy to Hosted canaries, monitor 30m, then promote.
Medium-term: add automated rotation test harness to CI that simulates leader handoff + clock skew and verify no dual-acceptance.
Long-term: add signed rotation events to audit logs + dashboard alerting per-org when >1 key accepted in rotation window.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy PR merged and built artifact includes sub-second precision fix
Auth-service PR merged and rotation flow emits monotonic markers
Canary rollout shows zero dual-acceptance incidents for 48h
Affected customers confirmed resolution or received remediation steps
Security review sign-off on token handling changes

notes: Affected environments: hosted, dedicated pools in us-west-2, private customers with older proxy builds.
Observed frequency: ~0.2% of rotation events during peak traffic windows; higher on Dedicated customers with asymmetric NTP configs.
Root cause timeline: introduced in edge-proxy build v2.11.0 (2026-01-27) where timestamp rounding changed to improve GC; regression not covered by rotation tests.
Non-blocking follow-ups: add rotation dashboard in Console + runbook updates for hand-rolled key ops.
